proposal.title: Certified-lower-bound decode admission with kill-and-restart into prefill-retained state for two-pool non-clairvoyant serving
proposal.hypothesis: In a two-pool simulator with unknown output lengths and decode memory overflow, decode admission that uses a per-request certified lower bound counter and evicts the smallest bound first lowers mean flow time by at least 5% compared with peak-reservation backpressure at a fixed maximum length. Both policies must have zero memory violations.
proposal.baseline: DMRS Algorithm 1 decode-admission step (2610.15579v1, lines 11-13): admit from W while sum of h_j plus h_i is at most M_D. Because h is unknown online, the non-clairvoyant instantiation sets h_i = p_i + u_max. This is the A_max analogue of 2508.14544v2. The strongest supplied non-clairvoyant control is A_min (2508.14544v2 Algorithm 2), applied to the decode pool alone.
proposal.operator_delta: Replace peak reservation with A_min-style lower-bound admission plus ordered eviction in the decode pool. The eviction transition is the new part: an evicted request's retained-cache location is determined by whether the prompt KV is still held in prefill memory, and that occupancy counts against M_P.

contribution_claims.text: State-transition rule: decode eviction returns a request to W only if its prompt KV is retained and counted in the M_P constraint; otherwise it returns to U and needs re-prefill.
Two-pool accounting simulator with projected-growth checks, reusing the corrected v2 peak checking.
Hypothesized at least 5% mean-flow gain over peak-reservation backpressure in tight-M_D, short-output-dominated traces.

mechanism_check.assumption_scope: A_min assumes one memory pool, a common prompt length s, and a known lower bound ℓ. DMRS assumes known d_i and instantaneous transfer. The target has heterogeneous p_i, two pools, and a retained cache. These are excluded regimes for each source, not contradictions.
mechanism_check.specialized_operation: Each slot: (1) for D, if the sum of (p_i + a_i + 1) would exceed M_D, sort D by õ_i ascending and evict until the projected sum fits; set õ_i to a_i. (2) An evicted request with a prefill copy kept goes to W and consumes p_i in M_P; otherwise it goes to U. (3) Admit from W in ascending õ_i while the sum of (p_j + a_j + 1) stays within M_D. (4) Prefill admits FIFO under the M_P constraint (1e).
mechanism_check.remaining_effect: If no prefill copy is kept, the policy reduces to A_min applied to the decode pool plus the DMRS prefill rule; the only added effect is cross-pool coupling. Whether keeping the copy beats re-prefill, given the M_P pressure it creates, is unresolved.
mechanism_check.simplest_baseline: A_min applied to decode with re-prefill on eviction. Its cost is repeated prefill compute; it has no M_P coupling.
mechanism_check.distinguishing_test: Run a matched ablation: retain-copy versus discard-copy under an identical A_min decode rule, sweeping M_P tightness.

evidence.supports: Waiting requests occupy prefill memory.
Ordered-eviction rule based on certified lower bounds.
DMRS memory safety is accounting, not allocation.

assumptions: Generated token count a_i is observable online.
Restart cost equals m_i for re-prefill, or a transfer cost for a retained copy.
Lengths are deterministic under greedy decoding.

data_paths.possible_leakage: The simulator oracle holds d_i. The policy must read only a_i and EOS events.

proposal.counterexample: Very long outputs and tight M_D cause repeated evictions. Wasted decode work then exceeds what peak reservation would idle, so peak reservation wins.
proposal.matched_control: The same simulator and prefill rule, with decode using peak reservation at u_max. A second control is A_min with discard-copy.

experiment.development: New synthetic traces with seeds not used in the serving-admission screens, two-pool, unit slots.
experiment.heldout: Freshly sampled seeds and a length distribution not inspected during development. Do not reuse the 180 exposed traces.
experiment.metric: Mean flow-time ratio per trace, median over seeds, plus a count of violations.
experiment.kill_threshold: Stop if the median ratio to the best simple control exceeds 0.95, or if any memory violation occurs.

proposal.prior_art_difference: Overlaps A_min (eviction by lower bound) and DMRS (retained cache). The unverified difference is eviction that targets retained prefill state. This is unlike the local largest-prompt screen, which changed only the waiting-queue order and had no eviction.

proposal.title: Geometric decode slicing with prefill-side retained restart
proposal.hypothesis: Applying GSA-style geometric response caps to decode admission, with killed requests returning to W instead of U, reduces mean flow time by at least 5% compared with full re-prefill GSA when M_P has slack.
proposal.baseline: GSA (2601.22996v1 Algorithm 2), in which killed jobs discard progress and restart. Restart cost there models re-prefill.
proposal.operator_delta: Change only the kill transition: when a decode job reaches its phase cap τ_p, its prompt KV is returned to, or kept in, prefill memory (W) rather than discarded.

contribution_claims.text: A kill transition targeting a retained prompt cache that is counted in the M_P constraint.
Hypothesized gain is limited to settings with prefill-memory slack.

mechanism_check.assumption_scope: GSA assumes identical prompts, an offline batch, and a single pool. Online arrivals and heterogeneous p_i are excluded regimes. The second source notes that relaxing these leads to hardness.
mechanism_check.specialized_operation: Phase p: run SPS with τ_p on D. When a job reaches τ_p without EOS, discard its decode tokens and move the prompt KV to W, which requires an available p_i in M_P (transfer back). Otherwise move it to U. The next phase uses τ_{p+1} = α·τ_p.
mechanism_check.remaining_effect: The saved compute is only m_i per kill. With unit-cost slots and m_i = 1, the gain is near zero, so the effect survives only when m_i is large relative to τ.
mechanism_check.simplest_baseline: GSA with re-prefill. Another simple option is keeping the prompt in decode memory, but that reduces k*.
mechanism_check.distinguishing_test: Analytically count kills times m_i against total flow time. Run the simulator only if that ratio exceeds 5%.

evidence.supports: Restart cost is re-prefill.
Kills are bounded per job.

assumptions: KV transfer back to prefill is feasible and costs less than m_i.
SPS can be adapted to heterogeneous p_i using a proxy prompt, as in 2607.09248v1.

data_paths.input: EOS events and the phase cap
data_paths.operation: kill and route to W or U
data_paths.possible_leakage: None if τ is set without oracle lengths.

proposal.counterexample: With m_i = 1 slot and transfer cost of at least 1, retention saves nothing and consumes M_P.
proposal.matched_control: The same GSA phases and α, with kills routed to U.

experiment.development: Fresh synthetic traces with m_i proportional to p_i.
experiment.heldout: New seeds and a different prompt distribution.
experiment.kill_threshold: Reject if the analytic saved fraction is below 5%, or if the empirical ratio exceeds 0.95.

proposal.prior_art_difference: GSA and Regime-Aware Routing supply both the slicing and the restart. The only proposed difference is the retained target. No local experiment tested this.

proposal.title: Arrow-style pool reallocation triggered by retained-cache pressure
proposal.hypothesis: Shifting memory or instances between pools when W occupancy exceeds a fraction of M_P improves mean flow time over static pools.
proposal.baseline: Arrow Algorithm 2, which flips instances based on TTFT/TPOT load (2505.11916v2).
proposal.operator_delta: Use the fraction of retained-cache occupancy in prefill memory as the flip signal instead of SLO load.

contribution_claims.text: A flip trigger based on the size of W.

mechanism_check.assumption_scope: Arrow uses stateless instances and SLO loads. Its flips already address decode overload, which is the cause of a growing W.
mechanism_check.specialized_operation: Each interval: if the sum over W of p_i divided by M_P is at least θ, flip a prefill instance to decode. In Arrow, high decode load (L_D ≥ L_EXPAND) already triggers the same flip.
mechanism_check.remaining_effect: A large W occurs exactly when decode admission stalls, which coincides with high decode load. After substitution, the signal mostly rescales Arrow's trigger, so it amounts to threshold tuning.
mechanism_check.simplest_baseline: Arrow P→D flip on L_D, which carries cooldown costs.
mechanism_check.distinguishing_test: Measure the correlation between the W fraction and L_D in traces. Do not proceed unless there are many cases where the two diverge.

evidence.supports: Arrow already targets this failure.

proposal.counterexample: Any trace where W grows only under decode overload, in which case the policy is identical to Arrow.
proposal.matched_control: Arrow flip based on L_D with the same cooldown.
proposal.prior_art_difference: Substantially overlaps Arrow and FlowKV's load-aware allocation. This candidate is threshold tuning.
